title: Atlas Retail — Edge VPC + Terraform upgrade playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Draft operational playbook and Terraform module notes for Atlas Retail (edge) private deployment. This doc captures sizing assumptions, network layout decisions, terraform module choices, a step-by-step upgrade plan from v1.3 -> v1.4 of the private control plane, and an explicit rollback/runbook for the on-prem environment in their three-edge-region topology.

High-level customer context:
- Customer: Atlas Retail (brick-and-mortar + kiosk fleet).
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC-connected dedicated appliances in each region), hybrid on-prem for certain PoS clusters.
- Compliance: SOC2/PCI scoped for payment interactions; no external internet egress from POS subnets.
- Expected QPS: 120 rps average, 500 rps burst (peak shopping windows).
- Model workload: 2 large gen models (latency-sensitive chat) + embedding pipeline (batching offline).

Goals for this plan:
- Upgrade the private control plane and runtime nodes from v1.3 -> v1.4 with zero customer-perceived downtime for inference endpoints.
- Introduce improved TF modules for nic/routing and idempotent firewall rules to reduce drift.
- Validate new quantized model bundle deployment path and rollback hooks.

Non-goals:
- Full re-architecture of Atlas networking. We'll keep existing subnets and route tables.
- Rewriting CI/CD for customer; we will supply TF modules and rollout guidance.

Assumptions (callouts):
- Atlas uses AWS accounts for each region. Terraform state is stored in s3://atlas-infra-tfstate with DynamoDB locking.
- Current control plane runs on g4dn.xlarge equivalent (NVIDIA T4) instances for model servers; we are moving to p4d-style inference nodes for throughput in region-1 only as pilot.
- Persistent KV cache backed by Redis (managed by customer). We will not migrate Redis in this upgrade.
- Customer agreed to a maintenance window for database migration steps: two 2-hour windows in UTC evenings.

Sizing summary (per-region):
- Region A (primary, downtown): 4 inference nodes (p4d.8x-ish) each with 1x A100-80GB equivalent GPU for high throughput, 64 vCPU, 1 TB NVMe for local cache and model store.
- Region B (suburban): 2 inference nodes, single 40GB GPU (A10G/T4-class), 32 vCPU, 512 GB NVMe.
- Region C (edge kiosk hub): 1 small inference node for routing/fallback with CPU-only worker for low-latency local decisions + 1 small GPU for periodic batch jobs.
- Control plane: 3 control-plane instances per region (small VMs, 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM) behind ALB and in Autoscaling group with min=2, desired=3 for redundancy.

Why this mix?
- Primary region gets heavier GPU capacity for real-time heavy gen workloads; other regions trade cost vs latency.
- Local NVMe to reduce model loading jitter during cold starts; we use the runtime prefetcher to keep hot weights local.

Network design notes:
- Keep existing VPCs. Create dedicated subnets: control-subnet, inference-subnet, infra-subnet (bastion/ansible).
- Security groups: allow inbound from customer application subnets to inference-subnet on ports 443 (API) and 2202 (internal model management). Control plane SG allows access from infra-subnet and Redwood management CIDR when permitted.
- PrivateLink: Recommend customer provision interface endpoints for S3 and ECR to prevent public egress for model pulls.
- DNS: Use Route53 private hosted zones per-account and per-region. Add TTLs = 30s for inference endpoints to support failover.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Use existing modules from repo: terraform-modules/aws/vpc, /asg, /autoscaling-gpu, /lb, /iam. Avoid forking; instead pin to tag v2025-09-atlas.
- New lightweight module: modules/inference/nodegroup. Purpose: encapsulate GPU AMI selection, local nvme allocation, systemd unit for runtime, prefetch task, and node labeling.
- Backend and locking: s3 backend w/ encryption, DynamoDB for state locking. Ensure modules that create Dynamo table are only applied once (root account ops).
- Example snippet to pin GPU AMI (keep as string, customer-specific):
    module "inference_nodes" {
      source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//aws/inference-nodegroup?ref=v2025-09-atlas"
      region = var.aws_region
      instance_type = var.instance_type_gpu
      desired_capacity = var.desired_capacity
      gpu_ami = var.gpu_ami_override # we hand customer a validated AMI ID per region
    }
- State migration: if Atlas currently has state in local files, run a one-off state mv to s3 remote and test lock. See linked PR in repo.

Upgrade plan (high-level steps):
1) Prep (T-7 days):
   - Run the terraform plan in a dry-run workspace. Confirm state backend access.
   - Add monitoring alerts for model-serving error rate. Create baseline metrics snapshot.
   - Validate image (GPU AMI) in a sandbox region with synthetic load.
   - Share change window with Atlas ops and obtain emergency contacts.
2) Pre-upgrade checks (T-1 day):
   - Confirm s3/dynamo locks are accessible from CI runner.
   - Confirm backup snapshot of control-plane DB (if DB used).
   - Drain one control-plane node and apply module to it to confirm idempotency.
3) Upgrade control plane (blue-green-ish):
   - Deploy new control-plane instances into infra-subnet (desired=3).
   - Register new control plane with LB; keep both old and new in rotation for 5 minutes. Gradually shift traffic using weighted routing (start 10% new).
   - Monitor request latencies and error rates for 15 minutes. If stable, increase to 50% then 100%.
4) Upgrade model runtime nodes (rolling per region):
   - For each region: add new node(s) with new runtime (v1.4) in ASG with desired capacity temporarily +1 (so we do not kill live capacity).
   - Warm model cache on new nodes using prefetch task (we'll upload model bundle to local NVMe).
   - Drain old node from LB (deregister target), monitor in-flight requests, then terminate old node when drained.
   - Repeat until all nodes are upgraded.
5) Post-upgrade validation (per-region):
   - Run synthetic latency tests (p95 <= baseline + 10%).
   - Run inference QA set to validate model outputs unchanged (or within tolerance).
   - Confirm embedding pipeline can still batch to offline workers.
6) Cutovers & cleanup:
   - Flip DNS TTLs back to normal. Remove temporary extra capacity. Create snapshot of final state and tag terraform apply with release tag.

Rollback plan (fast):
- If control plane regression with increased errors >= 3% p50 error, immediately switch ALB weight back to previous pool and re-register old control plane.
- If model quality regressions found, rollback model bundle to previous S3 key and drain new nodes.
- If autoscale misbehavior observed, increase min capacity to previous levels and disable scaling policies until fixed.

Testing checklist (pre-apply):
- [ ] TF plan OK with zero unexpected deletions.
- [ ] State locking verified from runner location.
- [ ] AMI tested under synthetic gen load for 4 hours.
- [ ] KV cache metrics baseline captured and retained.
- [ ] Observability dashboards (per-route) exist and have baseline.

Runbook snippets / commands:
- Terraform plan: terraform -chdir=infra atl.plan -var-file=atlas-region-a.tfvars plan -out=plan.tfout
- Terraform apply: terraform -chdir=infra apply "plan.tfout"
- To force state mv to s3 (one-off, run from admin machine): terraform state push -force ./localstate.tfstate -> not recommended; instead run terraform init -backend-config="bucket=atlas-infra-tfstate"
- Node drain (kubectl example if using k8s hosting): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Q1: Atlas is currently using a third-party NAT/firewall appliance that blocks some ECR endpoints intermittently. Do we add a mirrored AMI cache in S3 per-region as a fallback?
- Q2: For kiosk hubs (Region C) we recommended a CPU-only fallback; customer asked whether quantized models can run on CPU with acceptable latency. Need to validate in sandbox with the 1B quantized bundle.
- Q3: Who owns the DynamoDB table creation for state locks? Operations team or Atlas infra team? We need a confirmation to avoid accidental recreation.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Cold start spikes during initial rollout. Mitigation: prefetcher and extra warm capacity + low TTL DNS.
- Risk: Terraform drift in security groups. Mitigation: add automation to run tf plan weekly and file drift tickets automatically.

Appendix: quick terraform var suggestions for atlas.tfvars
- aws_region = "us-east-1"
- instance_type_gpu = "p4d.24xlarge" # change per-region overrides recommended
- desired_capacity = "4"
- gpu_ami_override = "ami-0abcd1234atlas-validated"
- s3_backend_bucket = "atlas-infra-tfstate"
- enable_private_link = true

Notes to self (Evelyn):
- Coordinate with Priya for compliance checklist (PCI scoping) before starting model bundle push.
- Validate the github PR that adds nodegroup module solves issue with race condition when attaching NVMe (see PR linked in this doc).

TODOs:
- [ ] Finalize AMI IDs for Region A/B/C and add to atlas.tfvars.
- [ ] Confirm DynamoDB ownership with Atlas infra.
- [ ] Run a full end-to-end rehearsal in sandbox with synthetic X-API-key traffic.

Relevant links and references:
- infra terraform modules PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/402
- Atlas private deploy confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/23456/Atlas+Retail+Private+Deploy
- Observability runbook template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/9981/Obs+runbook

End of draft.

(Feel free to leave inline comments — this is intentionally conversational; we'll formalize after the first rehearsal.)
